title: Understanding Generalization Requires Universal Induction
abstract: arXiv:2609.34458v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Classical statistical theory is insufficient to explain the successes of general-purpose AI models, because it depends on handcrafted inductive biases that it cannot justify. No Free Lunch (NFL) theorems force any learner that beats chance on some environments to underperform on others. We might hope that past experience informs which environments to expect, but NFL applies equally to meta-learning. Thus, any method that makes meaningful predictions necessarily begins with an inductive bias external to the data. Choosing to bias toward short programs yields Solomonoff induction (SI), whose performance is competitive against all computable learners - albeit up to "constants" that become large when comparing against specialized methods that exploit background information. translated_title: 理解泛化需要普适归纳
translated_abstract: 经典统计理论不足以解释通用人工智能模型的成功，因为它依赖于无法自圆其说的手工设计的归纳偏置。没有免费午餐（No Free Lunch, NFL）定理表明，任何在某些环境中胜过随机的学习器，必然在其他环境中表现不佳。我们或许希望过去的经验能指明应当预期哪些环境，但NFL定理同样适用于元学习。因此，任何能做出有意义预测的方法，都必然以数据之外的归纳偏置为起点。若选择偏向短程序的归纳偏置，便会得到所罗门诺夫归纳（Solomonoff Induction, SI），其性能可与所有可计算的学习器相媲美——尽管其中存在的“常数”在与利用背景信息的专门化方法进行比较时会变得很大。因此，我们将SI相对化到一个信息视角上，偏向于能够访问所有既有信息的短程序。这一做法重新框架化了归纳偏置问题（摘要原文在此处截断）。
tldr: 论文指出经典统计理论因依赖无法证成的手工归纳偏置而无法解释通用AI的泛化成功，并提出将所罗门诺夫归纳相对化到信息视角、偏向能访问所有既有信息的短程序，从而以普适归纳重新框架化归纳偏置问题。
en_tdlr: The paper argues that classical statistical theory cannot explain the generalization success of general-purpose AI due to unjustified handcrafted inductive biases, and proposes relativizing Solomonoff induction to an information vantage point—biasing toward short programs with access to all preexisting information—thereby reframing inductive bias through universal induction.
